mutant.description: A passing assertion never mutated has never been tested, and c24 now reads PASS on all six clauses -- so the live question is whether its comparison is real or vacuous. A sealed mutant was planted on a SCRATCH COPY of the check: after the chatter_window index is built, every table tone is shifted by +1.0, so the served value cannot match, and a live C1 must FAIL. It was run against --where local, NOT --where deployed, because section 1 constrains the deployed read to ONE invocation and a mutant run there would breach it; the clause machinery is identical in both arms and only the source of the served payload differs. The planting script asserts its anchor count is exactly 1 before replacing, then greps the written copy for the mutation marker, because a str.replace on a mangled anchor silently no-ops and the only symptom would be a check that still passes.
mutant.expected: C1 FAILS on all three windows with mismatches > 0, and C2 is untouched, since a tone shift cannot create an unreadable-table reason
mutant.observed: FIRED. 'MUTANT ACTIVE: every table tone shifted by +1.0'; C1 FAIL on days 30/90/365 with mismatches 51, 62 and 69, each example showing the served tone exactly 1.0 below the perturbed table value (e.g. 2317_TT_Equity 0.3099108735720317/3 vs 1.3099108735720317/3); R67 C24 SERVED: NO. C2 stayed PASS at unreadable 0 on all three windows, so the mutant hit ONLY the clause it should -- a specificity result as well as a sensitivity one. The counts are 51/62/69 rather than 95 because the tone comparison reaches only rows with voters > 0 and a non-null tone; a 0-voter row takes the 'no clear tone' branch, which a tone shift cannot move. That partition is explainable and expected, not a shortfall.

determinism.method: N/A. Two same-input runs of the GRADED read would mean invoking the deployed function twice, and section 1 says to read c24 on the deployed function ONCE. A second deployed invocation is therefore not available to this instance, and substituting two LOCAL-arm runs would be a different population -- it would measure the local handler's stability and say nothing about the deployed read being certified.
determinism.observed: Not measured, and deliberately not inferred. What IS known about the read's inputs is bounded rather than proven stable: the check resolves the LATEST chatter_window part, pinned in practice by the head-object on part-20261005T011931Z.parquet (13054 B, ETag e573a1f3e22b1c8ea3e7be2f655b3769) taken immediately before the read, and the deployed CodeSha256 was identical before and after. Those bound the inputs; they do not establish run-to-run determinism, and are not reported as if they did.
